answer: Give every agent a radio fingerprint, the way a harbor master knows each ship by its engine note. At enrollment the agent broadcasts a signed packet and nearby peers record the imperfections in its radio signal, unique to that one piece of hardware, in a shared vault. Joining also locks a $50 bond. Faking one identity means a new radio, about $40, and a fresh registration. Faking a thousand means $40,000 of radios and a warehouse to hide them in. Peers re-check the signal at random, and a mismatch burns the bond. Like timber, a fake identity rots fast, but a radio signature stays put.
